note.text: A summary condenses a source for a stated focus. Select central information and necessary qualifications, combine related points and express them concisely. Examples and repetition can often be omitted, but a necessary contrast or limitation must remain. A summary should not add a personal recommendation or reverse uncertainty into certainty. Any word limit must come from the actual task.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to retain central points while removing repetition, illustration and unsupported additions. Builds on: main ideas and text functions. Leads to: inference and paraphrase.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original source: A fictional club moved notices to a sheltered board because rain damaged paper. Members also copied announcements into a book. The trial made notices easier to retain, but pupils absent from school still needed another way to receive them. Summary: Sheltered display and a record book improved retention of club notices, though reaching absent pupils remained unresolved.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Identify the focus, mark central actions and results, then preserve any qualification needed to avoid distortion. Remove repeated examples before cutting essential meaning. Compare the summary against the source, not against what you wish had happened.

pick.q: Original source: The group labelled tools and recorded loans. Lost items were reported less often, but no independent count was made. Which summary is faithful?
pick.r: Labelling and loan records coincided with fewer loss reports, without an independent count
w: The trial proved no tool was ever lost
Every school must use identical labels
Independent counts confirmed a permanent result
e: Fewer reports do not prove no losses.
That recommendation is not supplied.
The source explicitly lacks independent counts.
pick.y: Preserve both reported change and evidential limit.

pick.q: Original source: Bih offered morning and afternoon practice. Attendance was higher in the morning; reasons were not investigated. Which summary fits?
pick.r: Morning practice had higher attendance, for reasons not investigated
w: The source proves household tasks caused absence
e: A preference or dislike is not established.
Attendance is not a learning-outcome measure.
No cause was investigated.
pick.y: Condense the comparison without inventing its cause.
